images.filename: Albany County DPW vehicles assisting with snow removal in the aftermath of the December 2022 blizzard, Michigan Avenue, Buffalo, New York - 20221228.jpg
images.caption: A pair of large dump trucks round the corner of Michigan Avenue and Northampton Street in Buffalo, New York, as seen a couple days after the end of a historic blizzard that brought four feet of snow, hurricane-force winds and whiteout conditions to the city. Staffed by volunteers from the Albany County Department of Public Works - among the many counties and municipalities from around the state who assisted in snow removal and other recovery efforts after what Erie County Executive Mark Poloncarz described as "the worst storm in [the] community's history, surpassing the Blizzard of '77" - these trucks will soon be loaded with cargos of ice and snow scraped from the city's streets.

images.caption: Pedestrians walk the streets of Buffalo surrounded by decorations for the Perry Centennial celebrations held in honor of Oliver Hazard Perry for his bravery during the war of 1812. The Arrases visited New York after their return from Europe in 1913. Edmund F. Arras (7/7/1875-10/19/1951), a prominent Columbus businessman and entrepreneur, founded one of the city’s first property rental agencies in 1892. Trained as a lawyer, he graduated from OSU law school in 1896 and went on to hold positions in numerous civic groups around the city. He was particularly active within Kiwanis International and was involved with several local religious organizations. In 1913, he and his wife Elizabeth traveled to the World Sunday School Association Convention in Zurich, Switzerland. They continued on to travel extensively throughout Europe documenting their journey through photographs. Due to the timing of their trip, these photos comprise a valuable collection of images of European cities later devastated by war. The Arras family’s lantern slides and negatives include images from their 1913 travels through US east coast cities, Atlantic islands of the Azores, Madeira, Gibraltar and the countries of Algeria, Italy, Switzerland, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, England, and Ireland. Also included are images from their 1920 train journey from Chicago to the western US for the Kiwanis Convention in Portland. These photographs include images of Chicago, Denver and western National Parks.

images.filename: Sisters of Charity Hospital, Buffalo, New York - 20200923.jpg
images.caption: Sisters of Charity Hospital, 2157 Main Street, Buffalo, New York, September 2020. The oldest hospital in Buffalo, Sisters traces its history to 1848 - the year after the founding of the city's Roman Catholic diocese - as a way of addressing both the general lack of organized health care in the city as well as the anti-Catholic sentiment that pervaded the city's institutional structure. An initial spate of controversy over the state legislature's use of public funds to prop up a religious facility was rendered moot by the hospital's exemplary performance during the city's 1849-50 cholera epidemic. The hospital's original location in what's now the Allentown neighborhood was superseded in 1876 by a larger facility at the corner of Main Street and Delavan Avenue (currently the site of Canisius College's Koessler Athletic Center), which itself was replaced in 1946 by the current facility.
